items.title: Claim and new-task compare-and-swap misses changes that land between the step-2 check and the recipe's own fetch, so claims and new tasks are silently overwritten
items.problem: Claim step 2 checks origin/main, then step 3 runs the section-11 recipe, which fetches again and builds the worktree from the new origin/main. A claim or `TASK-NNN: add` that landed between the two fetches is already in the worktree. The later actor overwrites status/owner/branch, or `cp`s the template over the new task file, and its fast-forward push succeeds with no conflict. The lost-update guard ('merge your intent into the new content') makes a claim win. The no-remote fallback lets a second agent commit inside the first agent's temporary worktree. This falsifies spec §12.8 ('the later claim push is rejected') and §12.2.2 ('works as a compare-and-swap'). Contract-level: J.4, D.4 step 6, M.2.
items.evidence: Scenario 1b (TASK-002): codex saw todo/none, claude-code then claimed and pushed, codex's recipe worktree already showed `owner: claude-code`, codex overwrote it and pushed `0a4027c..6a4b2b1 HEAD -> main` rc=0; origin/main reads `owner: codex`, two `TASK-002: claim` commits. Scenario 2b: ivan got TASK-005 from `next`, codex pushed its own `TASK-005: add`, ivan's `cp` overwrote it (` M docs/mkb/tasks/TASK-005.md`), push succeeded. No-remote: codex committed its claim in claude-code's clean temp worktree of main; `main:TASK-004` ends with `owner: codex`.
items.fix: Claim step 3 (RULES §5, spec §8.4.1, block item 3 and its P.1 copy): 'Right after `git worktree add`, re-run the step-2 check on "$d"/docs/mkb/tasks/TASK-NNN.md; if it no longer shows `todo` with `owner: none` or you, remove the worktree and pick another task.' Allocation step 6 (RULES §4, spec/04 §4.3): 'Create the file in "$d" only if it does not already exist there (otherwise allocate again), and commit only if `git -C "$d" status --short` shows `A` for it.' Lost-update guard: 'for claims and new records, a changed file means stop, not merge.' No-remote variant: drop the 'commit in the worktree that has main checked out' fallback for claims and new records. Update spec §12.2.2 and §12.8 wording and contract J.4/D.4/M.2. Mind the block's 35-line cap.

1) Claim. codex ran claim steps 1-2 and saw `status: todo` / `owner: none`. claude-code then claimed TASK-002 and pushed. codex ran step 3 (the section 11 recipe). The recipe's own `git fetch origin` built its worktree from the new origin/main, which already showed `status: in-progress`, `owner: claude-code`. codex set the fields and pushed `40bca16..111be51 HEAD -> main` with no rejection. origin/main now reads `owner: codex`, with two `TASK-002: claim` commits. An agent that edits by pattern instead of by setting the value would at least see its edit fail, but the rules do not say what to do then.

2) New task, the strongest case. claude-code computed TASK-006 with the §4.3 pipeline. codex then pushed its own `TASK-006: add`. claude-code's recipe worktree already held codex's file, `cp` of the template overwrote it (`git status` showed ` M docs/mkb/tasks/TASK-006.md`), and the push succeeded (`917ec57..0fe7f38`). origin/main now has claude-code's title, and codex's task is silently lost. Edit rights allow editing an unowned task, and the agent thinks it is creating a file, not editing one, so no existing rule catches this.

3) No remote. Once claude-code had committed its claim, its clean temporary worktree was the one "that has main checked out". codex committed there (rc=0), and `main:TASK-004` ended with `owner: codex`.

run4.sh confirms the fix works: a check inside the worktree where you commit catches both races, and anything later is still rejected at the push.

- The `A`-in-status test is redundant with the existence check.
- The lost-update guard can stay: the explicit steps are more specific and take precedence.
- Do not drop the no-remote fallback. In a repo without a remote, main is usually checked out in the primary worktree, so dropping it would make every coordination commit "ask the human". Checking in "the worktree where you commit" already closes the no-remote race I reproduced.

items.title: The PowerShell ID-allocation pipeline throws whenever at least one ID already exists
items.problem: `Measure-Object -Maximum` returns System.Double and the `D` format specifier accepts only integers, so `'TASK-{0:D3}' -f ($max + 1)` fails as soon as one task exists; it works only on an empty directory where $max is $null. The Q and ADR variants derived by substitution fail the same way. Every Windows/PowerShell adopter hits this on the second task. Contract-level: D.4.
items.evidence: RULES.md:135-141 and spec/04:85-90. Run verbatim in two adopted repos (6 and 5 tasks): pwsh 7.6.6 prints `Format specifier was invalid..`; Windows PowerShell 5.1 prints `Identificatore di formato non valido`. `(1,5,3 | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum.GetType().FullName` prints System.Double. With `([int]$max + 1)` it prints TASK-007 / TASK-006, matching `sh docs/mkb/tools/mkb-check.sh next TASK`.
items.fix: Replace the last line with `'TASK-{0:D3}' -f ([int]$max + 1)` in RULES §4 (and its synced copies in templates/minimal and examples/tarelog), in spec/04 §4.3, in every Q/ADR variant, and in contract D.4. Apply together with F03 (--no-renames) since both touch the same pipeline.

items.title: ID allocation never sees renumbered IDs: rename detection hides `git mv` targets from `--diff-filter=A`
items.problem: Allocation lists 'every file ever added on any ref' with `git log --all --diff-filter=A`. With a directory pathspec git detects renames, so the renumber commit (`git mv ADR-001.md ADR-002.md`, spec §4.4 step 3) is R, and merge commits are not diffed. The renumbered number is invisible to `mkb-check.sh next` and to the sh/PowerShell pipelines (which also lack a working-tree scan), so it is handed out again: a second collision. Breaks '1 + the highest number ever added on any fetched ref'. Contract-level: D.4.
items.evidence: concurrency-sim: after ADR-001 was renumbered to ADR-002 and merged, `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only --format= -- docs/mkb/decisions` lists only ADR-001.md; `sh docs/mkb/tools/mkb-check.sh next ADR` prints ADR-002; with `--no-renames` it prints ADR-003. checker-review fixture a5-next.sh: ADR-005 renumbered to ADR-006 on alice/adr-cache; `next ADR` on main prints ADR-006 (taken); patched copy with --no-renames prints ADR-007.
items.fix: Add `--no-renames` to mkb-check.sh line 54 (`git log --all --no-renames --diff-filter=A ...`), to RULES §4 step 2 and its sh and PowerShell pipelines (lines ~123, 131, 136), and to every allocation command in spec/04 §4.3 (step 2, sh, PowerShell, adopted-ADR one-liner); synced copies and contract D.4 likewise. Add a checker test: an ID created by `git mv` on another branch is skipped by `next`.

items.title: After a renumber, the mandatory rebase conflicts again and the cookbook steers the actor to rename the default branch's own ADR
items.problem: After renumbering, `git rebase origin/main` conflicts again (add/add) while `git merge origin/main` is clean. The merge-only exception lives only in section 11 and nothing on the branch records it. Section 1 step 1 (every session start), claim step 5 (takeover) and the recipe's last line all require a rebase. The cookbook maps the conflict to 'ID collision: renumber'; after `rebase --abort` the branch's ADR-001.md is main's accepted ADR, so step 3 (`git mv <OLD-ID>.md`) would rename main's ADR, breaking 'the item on the default branch never changes'. Forge rebase-merge of such a PR also fails. Contract-level: D.5, M.1.

Scenario 4: takeover per claim step 5 (`git switch -c ivan/task-002-queue-y origin/codex/task-002-demo; git rebase origin/main`) gave the same conflict; after abort, `git log -1 -- docs/mkb/decisions/ADR-001.md` shows `c87c091 TASK-001: use format X` (main's ADR).
items.fix: Renumber step 6 (RULES §4, spec §4.4): add a Watch out line to the handoff 'Renumbered <OLD>-><NEW>: take main by merge, never rebase'. Section 1 step 1, claim step 5 and the recipe's last line (RULES; spec §5.1/§8.4/§12.1): 'if `git log --oneline --grep="^mkb: renumber" origin/main..HEAD` prints anything, run `git merge origin/main` instead of rebasing'. Cookbook ADR row (RULES §11, spec §12): 'a branch that already has a renumber commit: do not renumber again; merge'. spec §4.4: 'merge such a PR with a merge commit or squash, not rebase-merge'.

items.title: Protected-branch claims: 'the older claim commit keeps the task' can leave two owners
items.problem: Protected step 3 resolves a race by commit date, but only the second pusher can see the other branch. If the first pusher's claim commit is newer, it has already checked, seen nothing, and started coding, while the rule tells the second pusher it keeps the task. Commit dates are client-set, can be skewed, and are rewritten by every required rebase. Contract-level: J.4a step 3.
items.evidence: prot.git with a pre-receive hook: codex committed its claim at 10:00:00 without pushing; claude-code committed at 10:00:30 and pushed; its step-3 fetch showed only its own branch, so it kept the task. codex then pushed; its fetch showed both, dates 10:00:00 vs 10:00:30, so by step 3 codex keeps it too. Both code TASK-004.
items.fix: Replace protected step 3 in RULES §5 and spec §8.4 with: 'Fetch again. If any other `task-nnn-` branch now exists, stop and tell the lead, whatever the commit dates; the lead assigns the task.' The later pusher always sees the earlier branch, so there are never two owners. Apply with F31 (prune and trailing hyphen) on the same lines.

items.title: README rule 3 makes every change look like a task, a branch and a claim, and the README never mentions the no-task case or the lite path
items.problem: A tech lead deciding in 30 minutes reads the README's seven rules and concludes all work needs a task file, a branch and a claim. The real rules are lighter: work finished within one session needs no task, the minimal profile allows trunk-based work, and small fixes take a lite path. The README mentions none of this, so the standard reads as the bureaucracy the brief warns against, and literal readers create a task per 10-minute fix (anti-pattern 33). Work that outlasts one session gets one task file and one owner, claimed visibly before coding, on its own branch (the minimal profile allows trunk-based work); work finished within one session needs no task: the commit is the record.' Add after the rules in the README: 'Small fixes (at most 3 files, no interface, configuration, schema or dependency change, finished now) take the lite path: check CURRENT's warnings and the docs for the files you touch, fix any doc you make wrong, update nothing else ([spec/05](spec/05-agent-workflow.md) §5.4).'

This is stronger than the real rules in three places. (1) RULES.md §5 and spec/08 §8.1 say a task is "NOT needed for work you finish in the current session (committed, and a PR opened where the project uses PRs); the commit or PR is the record". (2) RULES.md §14 and spec/11 §11.2 make one branch per task a SHOULD in the minimal profile: "trunk-based sequential work is allowed". The README's own Quick start recommends that profile by default. So "one branch" is flatly wrong for most adopters. (3) Running `grep -n -i "task|session|lite|small|trunk" README.md` finds no mention of the no-task case, the lite path or trunk-based work. The lite path is only in spec/01 §1.8 step 10, spec/05 §5.4 and the AGENTS.md block. Agents are not misled, because the AGENTS.md block carries the lite path and "Work that may outlast this session and has no task: create one". Adopters are misled. items.problem: `inl(l, v)` (line 89) tests `index(" " l " ", " " v " ")`, so any run of adjacent vocabulary words counts as one valid value and E3 'invalid vocabulary value' is missed for status, priority and profile.
items.evidence: a7-vocab.sh: `status: todo in-progress` and `priority: high normal` (TASK-003), `profile: minimal full` (INDEX), `status: accepted rejected` (ADR-001) -> `mkb-check: 0 errors, 0 warnings`, exit 0.

items.verify_reason:
I reproduced the problem. The checker accepts a value made of two valid words when it should report E3.

Where it happens: line 89 of templates/full/docs/mkb/tools/mkb-check.sh reads `function inl(l, v) { return index(" " l " ", " " v " ") > 0 }`. The checker uses it for status (line 149), priority (line 150) and profile (line 159). It also uses it as the gate for the rules that make keys required or forbidden by status (lines 241 and 247). Any run of adjacent words from a vocabulary list therefore matches. The same code is in templates/minimal and examples/tarelog, and all three copies have the same md5 (26a9c030...).

How I reproduced it: I copied examples/tarelog/docs to scratchpad/verify-F56/case and changed five values:
- TASK-006 `status: todo in-progress` and `priority: high normal`
- TASK-001 `status: in-progress blocked`, with no blocked_by
- INDEX `profile: minimal full`
- ADR-001 `status: accepted rejected`
- Q-002 `status: open answered`

All three checker copies printed `mkb-check: 0 errors, 0 warnings` and exited 0. As a control, a single bad word (`status: todoo`) is caught: `ERROR E3 ... invalid status todoo`.

Why it matters: contract L (the E3 row) lists "invalid vocabulary value" as an E3 error. Agents rely on the checker to catch a half-done status edit, such as appending the new value instead of replacing the old one. Such an edit passes silently today. It also skips the checks that depend on status: the TASK-001 case, "in-progress blocked" with no blocked_by, gets no error.

The fix works: I patched a copy (scratchpad/verify-F56/mkb-check.fixed.sh) and it reports all 6 errors, one per bad value. The unmodified tarelog example and the minimal template give the same results as before. The full template also gives the same results: 1 error and 22 warnings, from its unfilled placeholders. The existing suite (scratchpad/mkb-check-tests/run-tests.sh) plus the 4 new cases gives 683 passed, 0 failed over 191 cases. With the original checker, only the 4 new cases fail, 12 checks in total.

On the reviewer's fix: `[ \t]` is more than needed. A value's inner characters can only fail to match through a space, because the vocabulary lists are separated by spaces and the value is already trimmed. So `/ /` is enough.
